text:
sam: heads-up — the latency dashboard shows a weird tail for /v2/predict in us-west. p99 jumped ~3x around the time the new routing policy rolled out. raw request logs don't show long-running ops though. anyone seen this?
lee: yup saw it. looks like only manifests when we view the endpoint rollup, not when we slice by backend.
priya: interesting — is the rollup doing a naive sum of histogram buckets across shards? could be leaking mass between adjacent buckets when routes move.
mike: i replicated locally by replaying traces. when a small fraction of traffic hits a fallback path with slightly higher median, the merged histogram pushes the extreme percentile up even though actual slow requests are rare.
sam: so it's a rollup math issue, not actual user pain? we haven't had high error rates or support tickets.
lee: correct. ops traces show tail is from a different backend variant, but the UI label is the consolidated route, so it looks like the route itself regressed.
priya: quick sketch of the problematic query we run in the dashboard:
```
# pseudo-query
SELECT percentile_bucket_sum(lat_ms_hist) as p50,p95,p99
FROM metrics.requests
WHERE route = '/v2/predict'
GROUP BY time(1m)
```
The histogram union across label values uses fixed buckets and then recomputes percentiles. when traffic shifts between buckets, the union can create an artificial p99 spike.
elaine: this explains why slicing by backend_id removes the spike. the backend-level histograms are fine. aggregation is the culprit.
sam: what's the pragmatic fix? options I see: (1) store per-request latencies (heavy), (2) use streaming tdigest per-shard and merge (needs ingestion change), (3) make dashboard compute percentiles by weighting raw counts per-tag and only show per-backend rollups by default.
lee: (2) is ideal but touches ingestion. (3) is low-effort: add a UI note and change default view to "breakdown by backend" for percentile charts.
priya: +1 to changing UX default. also suggest a flag on the API/console to opt into "accurate rollup" which triggers a server-side merge path (uses tdigest) for teams that care about cross-backend percentiles.
mike: for the longer term we should add route_version or routing_hash as a labeled dimension at ingest time. then rollups are stable even during rollouts. downside: more cardinality.
elaine: agreed. propose this runbook: 1) change dashboard default to per-backend percentile view (UI PR) 2) add tooltip explaining aggregation artefacts 3) create telemetry ticket to prototype tdigest merge at ingest 4) experiment with adding routing_hash label behind a feature flag.
sam: can someone pick up 1 and 2 today? I'll file the telemetry ticket for 3.
lee: i'll do the UI PR (small toggle + tooltip).
priya: i'll draft the tdigest proposal and a rough estimate of ingestion cost.
mike: i'll prototype adding routing_hash as an opt-in label for a subset of traffic.
deploy-bot: deploy to staging succeeded for dashboard-ui toggles (canary=5%). :white_check_mark:
elaine: nice. follow-ups — we should add a short note in release_notes explaining this so PMs don't chase phantom regressions.
sam: thanks all. filing a short post explaining "why you saw a p99 blip" for the incident channel and linking the UI toggle PR.
lee: tagging @oncall just in case it reappears after the next routing change.
priya: fyi: this pattern could also affect quota billing dashboards if they use the same histogram rollup; worth a quick audit.
elaine: adding that to the telemetry ticket.
sam: done — ticket INF-4123 created with summary: "percentile artefacts from histogram rollups during routing changes". assigning to priya/telemetry.
